key_insight: PlenopticDreamer synchronizes generative hallucinations across camera views so that re-rendered videos remain spatio-temporally consistent in multi-view settings, overcoming stochastic divergence common in single-view generative re-rendering.
problem_solved: Maintains coherent, view-consistent hallucinations for camera-controlled video re-rendering across multiple viewpoints and time, reducing flicker and cross-view inconsistencies produced by stochastic generative models.
method: Camera-conditioned generative re-rendering backbone that supports multi-view inputs and explicit camera control.
Cross-view latent synchronization mechanism that aligns stochastic hallucinations across simultaneous views to enforce multi-view consistency.
Spatio-temporal regularization (consistency losses and/or attention-based fusion) that stabilizes hallucinated content over time and across viewpoints.
impact: Enables reliable multi-camera video re-rendering and novel-view synthesis with fewer artifacts and temporal discontinuities, making generative methods more practical for immersive content creation, VFX, and multi-view synthesis pipelines.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing inputs (multi-view cameras + target camera control), latent synchronization module, and re-rendered outputs.
Before/after frame triplets: independent hallucination vs. synchronized multi-view hallucination to highlight reduced inconsistency.
Timeline animation or flowchart illustrating spatio-temporal regularization across consecutive frames.
Quantitative bar chart comparing temporal and multi-view consistency metrics (e.g., PSNR/LPIPS/consistency score) against prior methods.
paper_authors: Xiao Fu, Shitao Tang, Min Shi, Xian Liu, Jinwei Gu
